Firm B always best-responds along its own reaction curve, but only where the two curves cross is A also best-responding, the Cournot-Nash equilibrium. Away from that crossing the market is not at rest: the firms take turns best-responding and the staircase spirals into the Cournot point. A Stackelberg leader instead commits first and picks the point on B’s curve it likes best, where one of its iso-profit curves just touches B’s curve.
